title: Hearing the Game: Audio Listener & Source
description: Understand the audio pipeline, the Audio Listener on the camera, and the Audio Source component for playing sounds.

slides.title: The Two Parts of Unity Audio 🔊
slides.content:
# Audio Listener & Audio Source

In Unity, to hear sounds, you need two essential components:
- **Audio Listener** – acts as the **ears** of the player. Usually attached to the Main Camera.
- **Audio Source** – is the **mouth** that emits sound. Attach it to any GameObject.

Think of a film set: the microphone (Listener) picks up sounds from actors (Sources). If there is no Listener, you hear silence; if there is no Source, there's nothing to hear.

By default, every new scene has an Audio Listener on the Main Camera. You can only have **one** active Audio Listener at a time.

quizData.question: What component acts as the player's ears in Unity?
quizData.explanation: The Audio Listener captures all sounds in the scene.

slides.title: The Audio Source Component 🎵
slides.content:
# The Sound Emitter

Add an Audio Source via **Component → Audio → Audio Source**, or drag an Audio Clip onto a GameObject (Unity creates the component automatically).

Key properties (in Inspector):
- **AudioClip** – the sound file to play.
- **Output** – the Audio Mixer Group (we'll cover later).
- **Mute** – silence the source.
- **Bypass Effects** / **Bypass Listener Effects** / **Bypass Reverb Zones** – skip processing.
- **Play On Awake** – starts playing as soon as the object is created.
- **Loop** – repeat the clip endlessly.

All these control how the sound behaves.

quizData.question: Which Audio Source setting makes the sound start automatically?
quizData.explanation: Play On Awake plays the clip as soon as the object is active.

slides.title: One Listener, Many Sources 🎧
slides.content:
# Scene Setup

- Each scene must have exactly **one active Audio Listener**. If you have multiple, Unity will warn you. The one with the highest priority or enabled last is used.
- You can have as many Audio Sources as you want. They can be attached to the same GameObject or different ones.
- The Audio Listener is typically on the Main Camera, but for a dynamic game, you can move it to the player's head.

slides.title: Pro Tip 🚀
slides.content:
## No Sound? Check Listener & Clip

If you don't hear anything, ensure the Audio Listener is active, the Audio Source has a valid AudioClip, its volume is > 0, and the object is not muted.
